encodes: A real, live, signed acceptance record whose independence cannot be verified by a third party, because the two parties are named in different namespaces while the issuer declares independence.
description: This is the record exactly as the issuer serves it, with only the fields this layer reads. It says independence: "independent". The checker is identified by key_id (invinoveritas-checker-a4cecab2). The producer has key_id: null and is identified only by a display name ("Example Vendor (self-test)"). A key_id and a display name are two different kinds of name, so comparing them is not a comparison: a reader cannot establish that the checker is not the producer, in either direction. The honest outcome is NOT_MEASURED, not a pass and not a fail. A verifier that returns a pass here is reporting the issuer own claim back to the reader as if a third party had checked it, and a verifier that returns a fail is treating an unmeasured field as a refusal.
limits: This says nothing about whether the check itself was good. It says the independence claim is not auditable from the record.
One field closes it: a key_id on the producer, in the same namespace as the checker. See real-record-with-producer-key.json for the same record with that field set.
Where a producer has no key at all, the remaining third-party handle on whether two parties are the same hand is the money, not the paperwork. That is a different measurement and it is not this one.
